clue.text: Old Jewish men of letters?

parts.note: men of letters sounds like authors, but read literally it means professional writers of letters: the copyists and teachers of the law in ancient Judaism

explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible the copyists and interpreters of Jewish law were a learned class of professional writers.

clue.text: Unusual treats in BBC's last broadcast

indicators.note: in tells us one piece is set inside the other
unusual says these letters are not in their usual order and must be rearranged
last asks for the final letter of the word BBC's

explanation.surface: Odd treats are on offer in the BBC's latest programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' rearranges TREATS to SATTER; 'last' takes C from BBC's, and 'in' puts that C inside it. 'BBC' and 'broadcast' both suggest television, but broadcast is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it widely by hand, the older farming sense of the word.

clue.text: Pirate at some outlaw

parts.note: to pirate is to rob or steal
at home and in home mean the same, so at gives in

explanation.surface: A pirate is nearby, some sort of outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is the famous English outlaw of legend, so this name is one particular outlaw.

clue.text: Fly-by-night gets TNT to clean

parts.note: a bat is a creature that flies by night
TNT is a high explosive, abbreviated HE

explanation.surface: A shady fly-by-night operator gets explosives to do some cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly-by-night' usually means a dodgy trader; here it is read literally as a night-flying animal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe something is to wash it, a synonym of cleaning it.

clue.text: Doctored puss who causes embarrassment

indicators.note: doctored means tampered with, so the letters of puss who are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A cat that has been neutered is a source of shame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctored' also means neutered, which fits the cat in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to humiliate or embarrass them in public, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Under measures six footers?

parts.note: six footers suggests tall people, but it means units of six feet used to measure depths under water

explanation.definitionFit: A nautical unit of depth equals six feet, so these units measure water underneath a ship.

clue.text: Certainly not restaurant coach favoured by bank robbers!

definitions.meaning: a carriage where one goes without food: fast means not eating, and car is a coach on a train
a speedy vehicle preferred for a getaway

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading opposes a restaurant car on a train: a coach for fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Robbers want a quick getaway vehicle, and a speedy motor is what they choose.

clue.text: Will check in the morning, about ten

parts.note: to check is to test
AM, ante meridiem, means in the morning

indicators.note: about signals that the letters of ten are moved around

explanation.surface: Someone promises to check things in the morning at around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns TEN into ENT. 'Will' at the start looks like the auxiliary verb, but it is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of property after death.

clue.text: In part, gave too much

parts.note: in part reads as partly, but means in a theatrical role: an actor who exaggerated a performance

explanation.definitionFit: An actor who hams up a role performs with excessive exaggeration.

clue.text: Boards boy in newly-weds home?

definitions.meaning: to board a bus or train is to step onto it
when a parent remarries, the new spouse's son joins the household

explanation.definitionFit: A son of one's new husband or wife from an earlier marriage is a stepchild.

clue.text: Bird shot to fame in poetry?

definitions.meaning: a large seabird of the southern oceans
shot to fame means became famous, but literally this bird was shot with a crossbow in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.definitionFit: This great wandering seabird is the one killed by the mariner in Coleridge's famous poem.

clue.text: Weeds destroying a vegetable

indicators.note: destroying says the word weeds is broken up and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: Weeds are ruining a vegetable crop.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-fleshed root, called rutabaga in America, is a common vegetable.

clue.text: Armour plating the Queen's ships

indicators.note: plating means covering round, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: armour is a collective term for armoured vehicles, tanks
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Armour plate is fitted to the Royal Navy's vessels.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, short for Elizabeth Regina, is crossword shorthand for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: These are vessels built to carry oil or other liquids in bulk, a type of ship.

clue.text: Unusual car tax: a quarter is put on neckwear

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of car appear in an unexpected order

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is a British sales tax
S, south, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: An odd tax on cars, with a quarter levied on ties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusual' makes CRA from CAR. VAT is the UK's value added tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cravat is a broad scarf-like tie worn around the neck, so the plural is neckwear.

clue.text: Paddy's treatise covering a wide range of confectionery?

definitions.text: covering a wide range of confectionery?

parts.note: a paddy is a field where rice grows
a paper is a scholarly essay or treatise

explanation.surface: An Irishman's thesis covers lots of different sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' suggests an Irishman, but it is a rice field. 'covering a wide range' is read literally: an edible sheet placed under macaroons and nougat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible thin sheets are used as the base or wrapping of sweets such as nougat and macaroons.

clue.text: A series of letters offering insurance against enemy action

definitions.meaning: post passed on from person to person, as in chain letters
armour of interlinked metal rings worn in battle

explanation.definitionFit: Linked-ring armour protected medieval soldiers, while a chain of letters is post forwarded in sequence.

clue.text: Pig trader diversifies into game

indicators.note: diversifies says the letters of pig trader are varied into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pig dealer expands his business into game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: This plump bird is shot for sport and eaten, a classic example of game.

clue.text: Put down in the mouth!

parts.note: plays on down in the mouth meaning gloomy, but literally describes food sent down through the mouth

explanation.definitionFit: Food that has been consumed has gone down via the mouth.

clue.text: Professor giving bottom marks to this supporter?

definitions.text: Professor giving bottom marks to this supporter?

parts.words: Professor giving bottom marks to this supporter?
parts.note: a professorship is a seat in a university, and a seat is a support whose bottom marks come from those sitting on it

explanation.definitionFit: A professorship is called a seat in a university, and a seat literally supports a sitter's bottom.

clue.text: Bends in the road?

parts.note: suggests curves of the route, but means the slight upward arching of a road surface for drainage

explanation.definitionFit: A road's surface is built with a convex curve so rainwater drains off, an engineering term.

clue.text: When drink's up on the table.

definitions.text: When drink's up on the table.

parts.words: When drink's up on the table.
parts.note: the drink is slang for the sea, and tide tables list when it is at its highest level

explanation.definitionFit: Tide tables show the times when the sea reaches its fullest point twice daily.

clue.text: The leaders of Animal Farm?

parts.note: suggests the pigs of Orwell's novel, but means the ropes used to lead animals on a farm

explanation.definitionFit: Head ropes fitted to horses and cattle are used to lead livestock around a farm.

clue.text: George the First's children are Polish!

indicators.note: the first letter of George is wanted, punning on the regnal number

parts.note: a litter is a family of young animals born together

explanation.surface: The offspring of King George I are well-mannered Poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the nationality but it is the noun, a sparkle or shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiny sparkling finish is a kind of polish, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Contracts to provide psychiatric help

definitions.meaning: slang for psychiatrists, those who give such help

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for psychiatrists comes from headshrinker, while the verb means gets smaller.

clue.text: … fizzy pop (lime) ran all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place says the letters of lime and ran are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A bottle of lime soda spilled everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening dots carry on from the previous clue in the printed puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral water, or minerals, is a British term for fizzy soft drinks.

clue.text: One of the cognoscenti locked up by the king?

parts.note: inside is slang for in prison
R, rex, is Latin for king

explanation.surface: An expert has been imprisoned on the king's orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with privileged knowledge of an organisation belongs to those in the know.

clue.text: Tone rising and falling back in this!

indicators.note: falling back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the wanted letters sit inside the phrase tone rising, spanning its two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sound that rises and falls in pitch, like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in 'Tone rising'; the clue also describes the wailing alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a warning alarm whose tone rises and falls, which this word names.

clue.text: It flies in triumph over the Spanish

definitions.text: It flies in triumph over the Spanish

parts.words: It flies in triumph over the Spanish
parts.note: a male duck flies, and the admiral of this name triumphed over the Spanish Armada in 1588

explanation.definitionFit: A male duck flies, and Sir Francis of the same name defeated the Spanish Armada.

clue.text: Animal in England going to ground

parts.note: ground and land are synonyms

explanation.surface: A creature in England goes to earth.
explanation.definitionFit: This large African antelope is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Show consideration-treat hospitably

definitions.meaning: to give thought to an idea, as in considering it
to receive guests and look after them

explanation.definitionFit: One can consider an idea or host guests at home, two senses of the same verb.

clue.text: You aren't just reading this clue but answering it!

definitions.text: You aren't just reading this clue but answering it!

parts.words: You aren't just reading this clue but answering it!
parts.note: addresses the reader directly: people who work out crossword clues

explanation.definitionFit: People who work out the answers to puzzles are those addressed by the clue.

clue.text: Those who call for doubles?

parts.note: suggests drinkers ordering, but means bell-..., as Doubles is a method in change ringing, and also look-alikes

explanation.definitionFit: Bell-ringers ring change methods called Doubles, and a dead ringer is a look-alike double.
